notes: v1.14.587 — POSE DETERMINISM. The locked rack pose is INSTALLED in bounded time instead of being approached over a frame count, so arriving at a rack lands the same camera whatever the frame budget. Owner ruling 2026-09-10, verbatim: 'rack pose: it's a real defect, the tolerance stands' — the tolerance did not move; the app did. Diagnosis docs/RACK-POSE-DRIFT-PHASE0-EVIDENCE.md. ONE VISIBLE CHANGE: none on the glass by design — this is a determinism fix behind an existing animation; what changes is that two arrivals at the same rack are now bit-identical rather than merely close. WHAT WAS WRONG: _ease converged 14 percent PER FRAME and set an axis exactly only once the gap fell under LOCK_SNAP (0.0009), so a walk-exit gap needed roughly 56 frames. At 60fps that is under a second; in the Playwright harness, which spec 37's own header records at ~2.7fps, it is ~21 seconds, and every frame the browser did not grant left the camera further from canonical. The RESTING pose therefore depended on the frame budget: 37-locked-rack-pose came to rest at -4.69565 against a canonical -4.7 inside a full 430-run while passing 4/4 in isolation. That violates the .455 ruling, which requires the pose be solved from the SELECTED RACK'S OWN TRANSFORM and never from previous camera state. THE FIX, and the option deliberately NOT taken: the ease factor is now derived from elapsed SECONDS (k = 1 - (1-0.14)^(dt*60)), so the same wall-clock glide lands the same pose at 2.7fps and at 60fps; a deadline (LOCK_EASE_MAX 1.6s, tracked in _lockEaseT) sets the pose exactly however few frames arrived; and dt <= 0 yields k = 0 rather than 1, so a zero-delta frame cannot teleport the camera. ⛔ RAISING LOCK_SNAP WAS REJECTED as the dishonest fix — it shrinks the residual while leaving the frame dependence in place, so the spec would go green while the property stayed broken. SECOND FIX, SAME CLASS, FOUND IN PASSING: lockUsableRect now rounds the measured rect where the measurement ENTERS. lockSync's change signature already rounded to whole pixels while lockDistance() consumed the RAW floats, so sub-pixel jitter in getBoundingClientRect moved the camera distance while the guard that exists to notice a change reported nothing had changed. ⚠ It is NOT the fix for the rack-pose failure — the rack normal is (0,0,1) so pos.x = at.x and the distance cannot move x — but it could move y and z between two arrivals at the same rack. UNTOUCHED: walk mode keeps its own per-frame orbit easing (camX 0.12, radius 0.08). It is a free-look mode with no canonical pose to violate, and test :179 measures AFTER leaving walk, which runs through the locked path this ship fixed. HARNESS, SAME COMMIT, NO APP EFFECT: 10-site-profile-root.spec.js:84 is RE-POINTED, not loosened. It asserted that migration seeds siteLead from the operator — behaviour v1.14.538 deleted on purpose, where dct-ios.html now reads 'Do not restore it'. The chain: .474's two-field cold open removed Site Lead from Site Setup, so the migration's 'a human states it in Site Setup' deferral pointed at a door that no longer asked, and the seed quietly became THE ONLY WRITER OF SITE AUTHORITY, granting it to whoever set the device up; .537 built the SITE/SYSTEM door Contract 9a names. The test now pins the stronger property — migration completes the profile (id, rootMigratedAt) WITHOUT inventing authority, siteLead() reports its absence honestly, and the ACTOR is still credited. It had been red since .538 and is recorded at PHANTOM_CURRENT_STATE.md:1476 as 'failing, not pinned'. ACCEPTANCE: spec 37 and spec 10 green in isolation (4/4 and 18/18), and the pinned baseline (docs/PLAYWRIGHT-BASELINE.md) re-run in full — isolation passed BEFORE this fix and proves nothing about it.
